symptoms: Dark green streaks appear on the veins of the lower leaf and stem.
New leaves are narrow, wavy, and struggle to grow.
Leaves have yellow edges and bunch together at the top of the plant.
Plants often fail to produce fruit.
If fruit grows, the hands and fingers are twisted and distorted.
Dark brown patches may appear on young fruit.
prevention: Always use planting materials that are free from the virus.
Keep your field clean and free of weeds to help spot infected suckers early.
Do not grow bananas near sugarcane or cucurbit crops to prevent virus spread.
practices: Remove and destroy all infected banana plants immediately.
Chop up, dry, and bury the infected plants.
Monitor the field regularly for signs of the disease.
